newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIAN TITLE DECIDER SET FOR ST PETERSBURG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIAN TITLE DECIDER SET FOR ST PETERSBURG.

text.p: Spartak Moscow will play defending champions Alania Vladikavkaz for the Russian league title in St Petersburg on November 16 after the two sides finished the season level on points, league officials decided on Wednesday.

League executive director Yuri Kaban said the play-off, the first of its kind in Russia where goal difference is not used to settle rankings, would be held at the Petrovsky Stadium where crowd trouble marred Spartak's final match last Sunday.

A league spokesman said Zenit St Petersburg had been fined five million roubles ($920) after the referee had to be escorted from the field by police under a hail of missiles following Spartak's 2-1 victory which assured them of a play-off place.
Defeat thwarted Zenit's ambition of finishing in the top eight, which would have clinched a hefty cash bonus from the city council.
The first victim was trainer Pavel Sadyrin, formerly Russian national coach, whose contract has not been renewed.
Sport Express newspaper quoted Zenit captain Vladimir Kulik as saying the players were dismayed by the board's decision.
